notes: Vitamin C reduces non-heme iron to its more absorbable ferrous form, increasing absorption 2-3x.
Calcium competes with iron for absorption when consumed together. Separate by 1-2 hours.
Vitamin D upregulates intestinal calcium absorption.
Vitamin K activates osteocalcin, directing calcium to bone instead of soft tissue.
Magnesium is required to activate vitamin D in the liver and kidney.
Zinc is required for retinol-binding protein synthesis; deficiency mimics vitamin A deficiency.
Long-term high-dose zinc (>40 mg/day) depletes copper via metallothionein induction.
Both support immune function; co-supplementation common in cold studies.
Selenium-dependent deiodinases convert T4 to active T3.
B12 is required to recycle folate; B12 deficiency causes functional folate trap.
Both protect lipid membranes; selenium-dependent glutathione peroxidase regenerates vitamin E.
At very high doses, vitamin A blunts vitamin D's signaling on the VDR.
Together direct calcium to bone and away from arteries.
Both reduce oxidative damage; lipophilic so absorbed together with fat.
